title: Degree-zero continuity for a canonical relative section cocone
statement: Let A be a Grothendieck abelian category, D:I→Sch a small nonempty cofiltered diagram of qcqs schemes with affine transitions, and c a qcqs limit cone. Fix a stage i, an A-valued small-étale sheaf G on D_i, and a qcqs étale object U over D_i. Evaluation at U of the explicit relative-section cocone from def-weil-pbc-grothendieck-etale-relative-section-diagram is a colimit in A. This statement involves neither hypercovers nor cochain complexes nor cohomology.

source.place: Detailed proof, paragraph 2: finite skeleton descent and finite-cochain section continuity; explicit categorical construction with Grothendieck coefficients.

external.place: Tag 09YQ, degree zero (abelian coefficients); arbitrary Grothendieck coefficients by the categorical finite-matching argument stated in the proof

proof.text: Choose a finite affine open cover of the qcqs etale object, and finite affine covers of its pairwise intersections. The constructed one-hypercover has finite matching shape. Apply the affine case on its components; the sheaf multiforks are limits at every stage and at the cocone point. AB5 and the colimit universal property prove the evaluated cocone is colimiting. The helpers finiteHypercoverColimit and qcqsColimitOfAffine contain this full categorical argument, including the empty-cover case.

For an affine etale U, restrict D to Over i and pull the cone back along U.hom. Initiality and connected pullback pasting prove the new cone limiting; affine transition maps make its stages affine. Explicit etale localization/global-section isomorphisms are compatible with transitions and cone legs, by the proved localization-unit and inverse-image composition calculations. Rebase the coefficient sheaf along U.hom using the proved inverse-image composition associativity, so the fixed base is the affine scheme U itself. A coinitial directed reindexing reduces the result to directed affine global-section continuity; finality reflects its colimit. The terminal-evaluation/ΓRes identity is reused directly from AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.terminalEvaluation_eq_res in EtaleObjectSections via a proof-only import all; no duplicate identity is declared.

lean.statement:
theorem relativeSectionCocone_isColimit
    {I : Type u} [SmallCategory I] [IsCofiltered I] (D : I ⥤ Scheme.{u})
    [∀ i, CompactSpace (D.obj i)] [∀ i, QuasiSeparatedSpace (D.obj i)]
    [∀ {i j} (g : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (D.map g)]
    (c : Cone D) [CompactSpace c.pt] [QuasiSeparatedSpace c.pt]
    (hc : IsLimit c) (i : I) (G : Sheaf (D.obj i).smallEtaleTopology A)
    (U : (D.obj i).Etale) [CompactSpace U.left] [QuasiSeparatedSpace U.left] :
    Nonempty (IsColimit (((evaluation _ A).obj (op U)).mapCocone
      (relativeSectionCocone A D c i G)))
